transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-08-05 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~60 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Maya Rivera (Lattice Head of AI); Tom Delgado (Lattice Eng Lead); Priya Singh (Lattice Security)

Summary (auto): Align on POC scope and timeline, confirm success criteria, access needs, and benchmark pass/fail.

00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Alex with Redwood, this is Samir our SE. Quick roll call?
00:12 Maya (Lattice): Hi Alex, Maya here, Tom and Priya both on. Thanks for doing this.
00:18 Samir (Redwood SE): Awesome, quick agenda — success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timeline/milestones, security questions.
00:30 Tom (Lattice): That works. We're mainly focused on latency for customer-facing chat and throughput for bulk summarization jobs.
00:45 Alex: Great, can you give rough numbers for QPS and interactive latency SLOs?
00:50 Tom: For chat it's ~50 concurrent users at peak, target 200ms p50 and 400ms p95 for 512 token responses; bulk summarization is batch jobs, approx 10k docs per day, variable size.
01:10 Samir: Got it, 50 concurrent is small but p95 400ms on 512 tokens is aggressive, we'll need to set benchmarks. Also want to confirm data residency — you mentioned EU-only?
01:25 Maya: Yes EU data residency for PII. We also need KMS integration and audit logs.
01:35 Priya: Correct — SOC2 controls, SSO, RBAC requirements. We'll need to review your attestation.
01:45 Alex: We'll include SOC2 summary and KMS options in the security pack, plus how Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment meets residency.
02:00 Tom: For the POC we prefer a Dedicated instance in eu-west, but open to a hosted variant if we can get the latency.
02:15 Samir: Ok we usually start hosted for speed, but for residency and network isolation Dedicated/VPC makes sense; we've done short Dedicated pilots in 1-2 weeks for access setup.
02:30 Maya: Timeline question — what's realistic for a 6-week POC with a mid-point review?
02:38 Alex: Typical 4-6 week POC: Week 0 kickoff and credentials, Week 1 access + perf baseline, Week 2-3 benchmarks and integration, Week 4 mid-point review with initial results, Week 5 remediation/optimizations, Week 6 exec readout. We can send a milestone doc.
02:58 Tom: That aligns. Key success criteria: p95 latency under 600ms for chat (initial), cost per 1k tokens under our target, and accuracy metrics for summarization (ROUGE/F1 baseline improvement).
03:18 Samir: We'll propose benchmark suites: latency run (50 concurrent, 512 tokens), sustained throughput test for summarization, and quality evals with your labeled set. Can you provide a sample dataset?
03:30 Maya: Yes we'll provide 1k chat logs (anonymized) and 500 summarization docs. We'll need NDA for data?
03:40 Alex: We'll confirm legal but we can proceed with anonymized synthetic data for initial runs; NDA can be parallel.
03:50 Priya: Also need IP allowlist and hostnames for outbound connections, and if Dedicated we'll expect VPC peering info.
04:02 Samir: For Dedicated we'll need a jump box and SSH keys, and we'll share a template network diagram.
04:15 Tom: Benchmarks — do you support continuous batching/kv cache so we can see savings?
04:22 Samir: Yes, Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching and batching; we'll include a config to toggle those and measure cost/latency tradeoffs.
04:35 Maya: On success criteria, exec readout will be to CTO + VP Product; they care about cost delta vs our current provider and risk (security/compliance).
04:48 Alex: Noted — we'll prepare an exec slide pack showing latency, cost per 1k tokens, and risk mitigations.
05:00 Tom: Who owns the mid-point remediation suggestions?
05:05 Samir: SE team will own initial tuning + suggestions; we'll list recommendations for quantization or model variant swaps and estimate impact.
05:20 Maya: About models — do you have performance profiles per model? We may want a 13B quantized vs 70B baseline.
05:30 Samir: Yep, we maintain verified profiles; for throughput we typically recommend a 13B quantized for chat to hit p95 targets with lower cost, and fall back to larger models for quality-critical cases.
05:45 Priya: Security question: can we bring our KMS and have keys in HSM?
05:50 Alex: We integrate with customer KMS and support HSM-backed keys for Private deployments; we'll include details in the security pack.
06:02 Maya: Ok great. One more — are there existing benchmarks or reference numbers you can share?
06:10 Samir: I'll share a benchmark spreadsheet with p50/p95 numbers across model families and hardware (A100, H100, etc.) but note noisy neighbors vary.
06:22 Tom: For the POC, can you commit to running identical traffic shape to our prod-ish sample?
06:28 Samir: Yes, provide the traffic shape and we'll replay it; we'll log token counts, latency distributions, and cost estimates.
06:40 Alex: Let's walk through milestones so everyone is aligned. Kickoff (week 0): introductions, legal/SOW sign, share infra requirements. Access setup (week 1): network, creds, sample data. Baseline/benchmarks (week 2): run initial tests. Mid-point review (week 4): show results and remediation plan. Exec readout (week 6): final slides and recommendation.
07:05 Maya: Sounds good. Can you send the SOW and a proposed kickoff date? We prefer 2026-08-12 for kickoff.
07:12 Alex: We'll aim for 2026-08-12. Action items captured.
07:20 Priya: On legal — we'll need SOC2 report and a data processing addendum before production; for POC anonymized data is fine but we'll still review DPIA.
07:35 Alex: Understood. We'll send SOC2 summary and DPA template.
07:40 Tom: For measurements, we need exported logs and token-level billing breakdown.
07:46 Samir: We'll enable token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards; we'll give you read-only access to console for the POC.
07:58 Maya: Good. Any concerns about running in eu-west?
08:03 Samir: No, we can provision eu-west Dedicated nodes; provisioning time for Dedicated is typically 3-7 business days once network details are provided. For hosted it is instant.
08:18 Tom: If Dedicated takes a week to set up, that still fits the 6-week plan if we start next week.
08:24 Alex: We'll include both options in the SOW timeline — expedited hosted baseline then switch to Dedicated when ready.
08:35 Maya: Metrics for success to confirm: p95 latency under 600ms for chat, summarization accuracy on labeled set within 5% of current model, cost per 1k tokens below our target (we'll share).
08:50 Alex: Perfect, we'll include those as formal success criteria in the SOW.
09:00 Tom: Who's point for infra coordination?
09:03 Priya: I'll coordinate from security side and Tom for engineering network details.
09:08 Alex: Great — recap of next steps: Redwood sends SOW + security pack; Samir sends benchmark plan and sample data template; Lattice shares anonymized samples and network diagram; schedule kickoff for 2026-08-12.
09:25 Maya: That covers it, thanks. Look forward to the SOW.
09:30 Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email and Slack.
